title: Unit – 2 : Session – 7 : SLO – 2 | Single Inheritance
sections: class Vehicle { String brand = "Honda"; void honk(){ System.out.println("Beep!"); } }
class Bike extends Vehicle { int gears = 5; void show(){ System.out.println(brand + " bike with " + gears + " gears"); } }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] a){ Bike b = new Bike(); b.honk(); b.show(); } }
Output: Beep! / Honda bike with 5 gears

Why single inheritance: Bike extends exactly ONE superclass (Vehicle). There is a single parent-child link, so it is classified as single inheritance — unlike multiple inheritance (one class, many parents), which Java does not support with classes.
